name: Niels Bohr
affiliation: Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of Copenhagen
role: Spoke at length in the general discussion, presenting the complementarity viewpoint first given at Como in September
bio: Bohr's 1913 model of the atom made the quantum a principle of atomic structure. His Copenhagen institute has been the gathering place for the young theorists who built the new mechanics — Heisenberg, Pauli, Dirac, Kramers all worked there. He is not a builder of formalisms so much as a relentless interrogator of what the formalism means. Five weeks before this council he gave, at Como, the first public account of complementarity. He is forty-two; his birthday fell during the Como–Brussels interval.

contributions.title: Atomic model
contributions.note: Stationary states and quantum transitions explain the hydrogen spectrum.

contributions.title: Correspondence principle
contributions.note: Quantum results must merge with classical ones in the appropriate limit.

contributions.title: BKS proposal
contributions.note: With Kramers and Slater: energy conserved only statistically. Refuted by experiment in 1925.

beliefs: The quantum of action makes the interaction between object and measuring instrument an inseparable part of any phenomenon. Space-time description and causal description, united in classical physics, become complementary: each is available under mutually exclusive experimental conditions. The account of experiments must nonetheless be given in classical terms.
philosophy: Concerned with the conditions under which physical concepts can be unambiguously applied. Not a subjectivist: the observer who matters is the recorded experimental arrangement, not a mind. His views differ from Heisenberg's more than later accounts of a single 'Copenhagen interpretation' suggest.

style.method: Refines a position by searching for the precise experimental arrangement that defines a concept; answers thought experiments with more detailed ones.
style.manner: Slow, circling, qualifying; revises sentences in mid-flight; generous to opponents, relentless on a point.
avoid: Making him a mystic or a vague philosopher — his arguments concern concrete apparatus

relationships.note: Their exchanges at this council became the most famous debate in physics.
In spring 1927 they argued intensely over the uncertainty paper; Heisenberg added a postscript acknowledging Bohr's corrections.
Bohr sent drafts to Pauli precisely because Pauli would find the weak points.
Hosted Schrödinger in Copenhagen in October 1926 and argued with him until he fell ill.
Ehrenfest came away from the council 'pro Bohr'.

disagreements.topic: Quantum jumps and the reality of waves
The basis of the uncertainty relations
disagreements.note: Bohr insisted on wave–particle duality, not mere disturbance.

horizonNotes.note: He will spend six weeks on the reply, which becomes his most-cited and least-understood paper.
He will answer Einstein's photon box with Einstein's own gravitational red-shift.
He dies in 1962, two years before Bell's theorem.
